messages:
ana: Heads-up — the sample 'bulk-embed' quickstart is spamming the hosted API and users are getting 429s during onboarding. Repro: the app fires 50 parallel requests for 50 texts on startup.

samir: Oof. Is it the SDK doing the parallelism or our sample app code?

ana: sample app. But the SDK doesn't provide any built-in client-side throttling primitives so folks roll their own naive Promise.all. Response headers show standard rate-limit counters + Retry-After in seconds. Example: 
`HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`
`x-ratelimit-limit: 120`
`x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`
`retry-after: 3`

morgan: That's bad for first-run experience. New users copy the sample and hit quotas immediately. Suggest we add an opinionated throttler in the SDK and a small helper in the sample that uses it.

samir: Agree. Proposal: SDK exposes an optional ClientThrottle that can be configured per-client with:
- maxRequestsPerSecond
- maxConcurrentRequests (semaphore)
- backoffFactor / jitter
- honorRetryAfterHeader (bool)

samir: Minimal pseudocode for sample app rate limiter: 
```js
// token-bucket + semaphore approach
const bucket = new TokenBucket({rate: 20, burst: 40}); // 20 req/sec, allow short bursts
const semaphore = new Semaphore(5); // allow 5 in-flight requests
async function sendText(text) {
  await bucket.removeToken(); // blocks until token available
  await semaphore.acquire();
  try {
    return await client.generate({input: text});
  } finally {
    semaphore.release();
  }
}
await Promise.all(texts.map(t => sendText(t)));
```

leo: Also make sure the SDK honors `retry-after` header on 429s and retries in a collision-safe way (not everyone retrying at same interval). Jitter is important.

ana: Another wrinkle: pagination endpoints (embeddings list, usage logs) return pages quickly so background sync jobs can still create bursts. We should document backpressure patterns: poll slower, use exponential backoff for cursor-follows, and provide a helper that converts a paginated iterator into a paced async iterator.

morgan: UX ask: sample app should detect when it's running with a demo key (low quota) and automatically switch to conservative defaults (rate: 5 rps, concurrency: 2) + show a warning banner in console. That will avoid most onboarding blowups.

samir: Implementation tasks I see: 
1) SDK: ClientThrottle primitive + honor Retry-After header + default jittered backoff policy (configurable)
2) Samples: replace Promise.all usage with the provided throttle helper
3) Docs: add a "Rate limits and client-side throttling" page with recipes (bulk inference, pagination, background sync)
4) Tests: simulate 429 and check SDK waits for Retry-After and doesn't spin up retries

devx-bot: Created TICKET #4567: 'SDK: Add client-side throttling & Retry-After handling' assigned to @samir, due next week. Link: https://redwood.example/t/4567

ana: One more thing — telemetry: it would help if the SDK emitted a metric/event when it hits a local throttle (so we can track how often samples are being rate-limited). Anonymous by default.

leo: Good idea. Also expose a small debug mode that logs when tokens are queued/delayed for easier dev debugging.

morgan: I'll update the sample app PR if you want. I can swap out the naive parallel logic and wire the conservative demo-key defaults.

samir: Please do — that + SDK change should reduce onboarding 429s dramatically. Thanks! :thumbsup:

ana: Thanks team. I'll follow up with a short doc snippet we can paste into the quickstart. :raised_hands:
